identity.title: [C II] Line Emission in Massive Star-forming Galaxies at z = 4.7

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the [CII] 157.7$\mu$m fine structure line and thermal dust continuum emission from a pair of gas-rich galaxies at $z=4.7$, BR1202-0725.

targets.name: BR1202-0725 (North SMG, South quasar host, SW companion)

evidence.quote: These are separated by 3.8$''$ (25 kpc) in the North-West direction
These are separated by 3.8$''$ (25 kpc) in the North-West direction

question.value: What are the [CII] line and 340 GHz dust continuum properties of the quasar host, the SMG and a faint companion in BR1202-0725 at z=4.7, and how do their [CII]/FIR ratios compare with other high-z systems?

evidence.quote: In this work, we present observations of the thermal dust continuum and redshifted [CII] line emission in the quasar host galaxy, BR1202-0725 at $z = 4.7$
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00006.SV.
The BR1202-0725 system was observed at 335 GHz (Band 7) with 17 12-m diameter antennas

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spectral windows of 1.875 GHz (7.5 GHz total); channel spacing 15.6 MHz (~14 km/s) at 334.96 GHz

evidence.quote: The total bandwidth of these observations was 7.5 GHz, divided into four spectral windows of width 1.875 GHz.
The correlator channel spacing was 15.6 MHz, corresponding to $\sim$14 km s$^{-1}$ at the observed frequency of 334.96 GHz.
The rest frequency of the [CII] line is 1900.539 GHz.
17 12-m diameter antennas of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array as part of science verification on January 16, 2012

configurations.value: mostly compact, two antennas on longer baselines

evidence.quote: Most of the antennas were in a compact configuration with two antennas on longer baselines
providing a maximum baseline length of $\sim$350-m
The synthesized beamsize of the 340 GHz continuum observations is $1.30'' \times 0.86''$

sensitivity.value: continuum 0.2 mJy/beam at 340 GHz; channel rms 2.0 mJy/beam at ~28 km/s

evidence.quote: which results in a 340 GHz continuum sensitivity of 0.2 mJy per beam
the channel rms is 2.0 mJy per beam

as part of science verification on January 16, 2012

method.value: Image last three spectral windows; Gaussian fitting in image plane

Gaussian fitting of the continuum emission in the image plane

validation.value: Total 43 mJy agrees with SCUBA 850 um 42 mJy

evidence.quote: in excellent agreement with the previous $\sim$14$''$ resolution 850 $\mu$m SCUBA observations

method.value: Spectra extracted at continuum peak positions from continuum-subtracted cubes; Gaussian fits for z, FWHM and integrated flux

evidence.quote: From the spectral line data cubes we extract spectra at the positions of peak intensity in the submm image.
We fit Gaussian line profiles to the two detected [CII] lines and the results are given in Table 1.

validation.value: Compared with CO line widths and SMA [CII] of Iono et al.

evidence.quote: The [CII] linewidth and redshift of BR1202-0725 North are in agreement with the previous SMA observations of Iono et al. (2006).

method.value: Adopt Iono et al. L_FIR for North and South, checked with greybody scaling; SW scaled by flux density ratio; compute L_[CII] from line flux

evidence.quote: we scale down the luminosities of the two bright sources by the ratio of the flux densities, implying $L_{\rm FIR} \sim 10^{12}$ L$_{\odot}$

assumptions.value: beta = 1.5; dust T = 35 K (SMG), 60 K (quasar); cosmology (0.73, 0.27, 0.71)

evidence.quote: assuming $\beta = 1.5$ with dust temperatures of 35 K for the SMG (e.g. Kovacs et al. 2006) and 60 K for the quasar

validation.value: Reproduces combined 350 um flux density of the pair

evidence.quote: simultaneously reproduce the combined 350 $\mu$m flux density of the pair (Benford et al. 1999)
Data analyis was performed using the *CASA* software package
$L_{\rm [CII]}/L_{\rm FIR} = (8.3\pm 1.2)\times 10^{-4}$ for the starburst SMG to the North
$L_{\rm [CII]}/L_{\rm FIR} = (2.5\pm 0.4)\times 10^{-4}$ for the quasar host galaxy
The total 340 GHz flux density of the system is $43\pm 6$ mJy (including calibration uncertainties)

findings_qualitative.value: Tentative broad positive-velocity [CII] wing in the quasar, possibly a single-sided outflow

evidence.quote: however a low intensity, broad line width extension is seen toward positive velocities.

claims.hypothesis: Is [CII]/FIR lower in the quasar host than in the starburst SMG?
claims.experiment: Measure [CII] and 340 GHz continuum in both components and combine with L_FIR
claims.finding: Consistent with lower ratios in quasars than starbursts

evidence.quote: in agreement with previous high-redshift studies that suggest lower [CII]-to-FIR luminosity ratios in quasars than in starburst galaxies

claims.hypothesis: Is there an overdensity of massive IR-luminous galaxies around BR1202-0725?
claims.experiment: Continuum detection of a third source and comparison with SMG number density
claims.result: Two SMG-like galaxies within 25 kpc; faint third source detected

evidence.quote: the quasar and the SMG represent an overdensity of massive, infrared luminous star-forming galaxies within 1.3 Gyr of the Big Bang

limitations_admitted.value: Lack of Tsys and WVR in the data adds 15% flux uncertainty; SW redshift unknown; outflow needs higher resolution

evidence.quote: Some uncertainty in the flux density of 3C279 is present due to the lack of system temperature measurements with these data.

referee_caveats_inferred: L_FIR mostly adopted from literature with assumed dust temperatures
Overdensity claim rests on SW source with unknown redshift
